Station 03 · Computer controls

Controls Lab

Recognise the computer, find the key Windows features and choose the correct mouse action.

Desktop or laptop?

Know your kit

A desktop has separate parts. A laptop combines the computer, screen and keyboard in one portable device.

Both are computersThey run applications, open files and create work.
Controls differA laptop may use a touchpad instead of a mouse.

Four Windows landmarks

Recognise, do not memorise
▦Windows desktopThe main workspace that appears after you sign in.
⊞Start menuFind applications, settings and power.
━TaskbarShows open and pinned applications.
📁File ExplorerFinds and opens files and folders.

Match the mouse action

Required

Choose the best action for each task.

1
Select a button once
2
Open a desktop icon
3
See more options for an item
4
Move down a long page
5
Move an item to a new position

Mouse guide

Useful detail: a desktop icon normally opens with a double left-click, but a taskbar icon normally needs only one left-click.

Explorer field guide

Key terms

Desktop computerA computer normally used in one place, often with a separate monitor, keyboard and mouse.
LaptopA portable computer with the screen, keyboard, touchpad and computer combined.
Windows desktopThe main on-screen workspace that appears after signing in.
Start menuA Windows menu used to find applications, settings and power options.
TaskbarThe strip, usually at the bottom of the screen, showing open or pinned applications.
File ExplorerThe Windows tool used to find and open files and folders.
Right-clickPress the right mouse button once to show a context menu with extra options.
Drag and dropHold an item with the mouse, move it to a new place and release it.
DownloadCreate or receive a copy of a file on the computer. In this lesson, both the chosen image and workbook are downloaded to My Documents.
UploadSend a file from the computer into an online service, such as attaching work to a Google Classroom assignment.
Turn inSubmit the attached work to the teacher after checking that the correct file has finished uploading.
ScreenshotAn image showing what was visible on the computer screen at a particular moment.
ClipboardThe temporary place where copied or cut content waits before it is pasted.
Keyboard shortcutA combination of keys that performs an action without using menus.
Sign outEnd your account session so the next person cannot access your work or personal information.
Acceptable useThe school expectations and policy for using accounts, equipment, networks and software safely, responsibly and for authorised purposes.
